guide.item_info_desc:
Experience potions can be purchased at the shop and used directly on your characters.
Compare the efficiency of each potion (experience / price) to make the best choice.

Shop Composition: Each visit generates 3 characters + 2 potions randomly.
Potion selection probability is determined by the weight field.
guide.efficiency_desc:
✓ Recommended: All experience potions have excellent efficiency.
If you have enough gold, start with the large potion.

Efficiency Standards:
- Large (🏺): 1.67 EXP/G - Best efficiency
- Medium (⚗️): 1.50 EXP/G - Medium efficiency
- Small (🧪): 1.25 EXP/G - Basic efficiency
guide.stage_difficulty_desc:
Difficulty is calculated based on enemy stat scaling (sm.hp, sm.atk) and enemy count.
Designed with gradually increasing difficulty, with Stage 10 being the hardest.

Stage 1-2: Beginner difficulty (0.65x)
Stage 3-4: Intermediate difficulty (0.8~0.9x)
Stage 5-6: Intermediate-Advanced difficulty (0.95x)
Stage 7-8: Advanced difficulty (1.0x)
Stage 9-10: Expert difficulty (1.1~1.15x)
guide.resource_system_desc:
Fury — MAX: 10~5 | +1 on attack, +2 on hit | Skills: Strike(3), Switch(1), Pierce(5)
Passive: warrior Rampage(ATK×1.5), knight Counter(Adjacent enemy ATK×50% counterattack)

Energy — MAX: 100 | Auto-recover +resRec per turn | Skills: Leap(20), Assault(40), Assassinate(60)
Bonus: Assassins recover 2x energy in forests

Mana — MAX: 100~120 | Starts at MAX in battle | Recover +resRec per turn
Uses: Fireball(40), Group Heal(50)

g.title: Strategy Guide
g.sub: How to lead the Solbit clan through all 100 stages
g.story_p: Fifteen years ago, on the Night the Sky Split, a child with a split-star scar on one palm was found in the rubble. That child grows up to become the Commander of the militia of Solbit Village. Together with the clan members, the Commander crosses a world crumbling under frost, plague and fire to lock the Demon Lord's gate. Scenes play before and after stages and during battles, and you can rewatch them with Story Replay on the stage select screen.
g.hero_p: Choose male or female and rename freely. Navy uniform, gold epaulettes and a silver baton. A commander who never goes onto the field but reads the battle from the rear and gives orders, so the Commander is never in the battle party. The baton was handed down by Bram, a symbol of one who only commands.
g.cast_bram_p: The militia's drillmaster. A former royal knight who calls the Commander "kid". Suspicious of the Royal Archmage from the very start.
g.cast_sera_p: "If you get hurt, I'll fix you up." A kind healer who works herself to exhaustion. She clashes with the Commander over the evacuation, and both grow from it.
g.cast_bark_p: A brawler who turned bandit out of hunger. Taken in by the Commander at stage 5, he becomes the clan's mood-maker.
g.cast_kasha_r: Rival · Leader of the Black Feather
g.cast_kasha_p: A rival who sneers at the "country commander" and turns every mission into a race. Fighting side by side, she slowly becomes a true comrade.
g.cast_ordin_p: The Royal Archmage who sponsors the clan. Shows an unusual interest in the Commander's scar.
g.boss_p: Every boss is tied to the story. The number is the stage.
g.boss_10: Leader of the bandit fortress. Got his weapons from a mysterious mage.
g.boss_20: A frozen royal knight — Halvar, Bram's old comrade-in-arms.
g.boss_30: A swamp summoner spreading plague through Blackwater Marsh.
g.boss_40: The emperor who made a pact: "Feed the fire and you'll get a new world."
g.boss_45: A gatekeeper of the Abyss, hunting the Key.
g.boss_50: A towering warrior guarding the road through the Abyss.
g.boss_60: Guardian of the Hell Gate, which only the Key's blood can pass.
g.boss_70: A demon sorcerer who shakes the heart with illusions.
g.boss_80: A summoner calling the god from the top of the sky.
g.boss_90: A demon general marching on Solbit, the Commander's home.
g.boss_92: The Lord's first sword — once a human knight.
g.boss_94: A summoner of an endless horde.
g.boss_95: A demon who wished to be human. Asks: "What is a human?"
g.boss_99: The last shield guarding the Lord.
g.boss_100: The Demon Lord whose gate the Sealers locked fifteen years ago.
g.spoil_1: The Commander's parents were royal Sealers who closed the rifts in the sky. The scar marks that bloodline — the Key that opens and shuts the gate.
g.spoil_2: In Ep5 (stage 49), Bram reveals the truth and falls holding the retreat alone.
g.spoil_3: Ordin is the mastermind who abandoned the Sealers fifteen years ago. He plans to open the Hell Gate and summon the god — he is the Summoner of the God at stage 80.
g.spoil_4: The Commander spares the defeated Ordin, who in the end atones by breaking the throne's final seal with his own life.
g.spoil_5: In the finale, the Commander lays down the baton, and every clan member places a hand together to turn the Key as one.
g.overview_p: Lead 5 clan members through 10 episodes and 100 stages. A boss appears every 10 stages, and the final episode has bosses back to back. The commander (protagonist) leads from the rear and does not fight.
g.overview_warn: Enemies grow exponentially. Levels alone won't keep up — you need promotions, skills, gear, combo buffs and tactics.
g.first1_p: Turn two novices into a knight and a priest at the Academy. A knight that holds and a priest that heals survive the longest.
g.first2_p: Later on, classes that hit many foes at once like the mage shorten battles. The research bot went furthest with knight · priest · mage ×3.
g.first3_p: New members join on the first clear of stages 2, 4, 6, 8 and boss stages. You can also hire mercenaries and buy class scrolls.
g.daily1_p: Drops soul fragments, enhance stones and class set gear. Pick the highest difficulty unlocked.
g.daily2_p: It refreshes every hour. Buy key skill books and class scrolls for your main classes first.
g.level_tip: At the level cap a member stops gaining EXP — later on, promotion is growth. Kill EXP is split among survivors, so fewer deaths means faster growth.
g.promote_li1: Sacrifice members of the same class to reach 4 points: higher grade 4 · same grade 2 · one grade lower 1.
g.promote_soul: C→B needs no soul stones; B→A needs {a} of that class and A→S needs {b}.
g.promote_li3: Each sacrifice raises the target's base skill by +1.
g.promote_note: Soul stones come from daily dungeons (10 class fragments = 1), first boss clears and the shop. Feed the tank first, then your main damage dealer.
g.gold_1: Revive — first, whenever a main member falls
g.gold_2: Core roster — class scrolls, mercenaries, same-class sacrifices for promotion
g.gold_5: Enhance gear — get stones by dismantling spare gear
g.gold_warn: Wipe → instant retry is the most common losing pattern. Earn gold in practice mode (cleared stage info window), revive your core, then try again.
g.wpn_p: Warrior greatsword, knight sword, mage staff… one weapon line per class.
g.arm_p: Cloth · leather · chain · plate. Each type can be worn by certain classes.
g.copt_tip: Class options (blue lines) only work on that class. On other classes they turn grey, so match the gear to the option's class.
g.break_p: Each failure has a 0.5% chance to break the item. Repairing with gold resets it to +0 and removes enhancement options. A Protection Scroll prevents breaking on that attempt.
g.eopt_p: Success may add a gold option (guaranteed at +10). Losing a level removes that level's option.
g.tip1: Dismantle, don't sell. Common gear sells for 30G, but dismantling gives an enhance stone (200G in the shop).
g.tip2: Failures don't drop levels up to +3, so bring all main gear to +3 first.
g.tip4: Protection Scrolls are worth it on +8 and above.
g.leg_p: Drops from boss stages and hell daily dungeons. Legendaries you don't own come first; dismantling gives a Legend Shard, and 5 shards buy the one you want.
g.set_p: Helmet, armor and boots drop in that class's daily dungeon. With 2+ members in a full set, the combo buff gets a step stronger through resonance.
g.more_gear: See the full list in Compendium → Gear.
g.syn_p: Your lineup grants party-wide buffs: 5 of one class gives a strong specialty, 3 a small one, and role mixes add balance buffs.
g.t2: Flank · pincer|+15% · +20%|Pincer when an ally is on the opposite side
g.t3: High ground|+15%, ranged range +1|Ranged dealers on hills
g.t4: Forest|15% dodge vs basic attacks|Park ranged dealers in forests
g.t6: Cover · intercept|Units behind a knight can't be targeted in melee; the knight takes ranged hits at 50%|Shield the back line with a knight (assassins ignore cover)
g.t7: Vault|Archers and assassins vault over an ally for +2 tiles|Jump behind enemies for rear attacks
g.t8: Shove|Push an enemy 1 tile; collision damage if blocked|Knights resist 70% of the time
g.t9: Defend · overwatch|DEF ×1.5 · shoot approaching foes first|Tanks with nowhere to go · waiting ranged units
g.def_p: Enemies crossing the wall build up breaches; if a quarter break through, you lose. Block the gate with a knight.
g.off_p: Every map has at least one 2-tile-wide path from your side to the enemy's. Siege tools are for shortcuts.
g.star_p: ★2 no deaths, ★3 within the turn limit. Each new star gives bonus gold.
g.hz_p: Each map type imposes a penalty on clan members. Members wearing any gear with the matching defense enchant are unaffected.
g.hz_tip: Many late stages are hell maps, so fire ward is the most used. The research bot also died most on hell maps.
g.ench1: Engrave at Sanctuary → Enchant for 1 rune + 100G. The rune is consumed.
g.ench2: An item can hold one defense + one offense enchant; another rune of the same category overwrites it.
g.ench3: Check the next few maps and ward the tank first, then the back line. Lifesteal and thunder are solid offense runes.
g.chest_p: 1~2 chests appear mid-map each battle and open when stepped on; loot is kept even if you lose. Grab them on the way, but don't break formation for them.
g.r1: Turn two novices into a knight and a priest first. New members join on the first clears of stages 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10.
g.r2: Clearing stage 20 unlocks normal daily dungeons. Start collecting soul stones and prepare for snow and ruins maps.
g.r3: Casualties start in earnest. Assassins ignore cover and hunt the back line — keep someone next to the priest. Use poison wards in swamps and jungles.
g.r4: Enemy mages multiply. Stand in forests and spread out to reduce area damage. Bring main gear to +3.
g.r5: Hell maps become common and enemy attack jumps. Clearing 45 unlocks hard daily dungeons. Rush A→S promotions and fire wards.
g.r6: Enemy numbers stop growing, but each hit hurts. Battles running past 10 minutes mean you're underpowered.
g.r7: Maps vary a lot, so re-engrave defense runes per map. Area damage lineups are fastest.
g.r8: You need S grades, key skills at Lv10, enhanced gear and combo buffs. Boss stages have fewer but elite enemies.
g.r9: Before the final episode, aim for legendaries and class set resonance.
g.r10: Back-to-back bosses at 92~95, 99 and 100. Don't hold back heals and Defend so your tank stays up.
g.b1: Knight·Priest·Mage×3|S100 clear|Area magic: shortest battles, went furthest
g.b2: Knight·Priest·Archer×3|S80|Ranged firepower; longer with many foes
g.bot_note: The bot plays simpler tactics than a person. If battles drag past 10 minutes, it's a sign you're underpowered — get stronger through daily dungeons, promotions and enhancing before pushing on.
g.foot: Numbers come straight from the game data · full lists in the Compendium
